answer: Each identity answers epoch-seeded timing challenges from three dispersed beacons: a zephyr-fast reply proves a distinct network location, since one machine cannot fake three low-latency paths. Signed replies are checked against a tide of recent RTT baselines, so a farm in one data center shows clustered latencies. The nebula of beacons rotates each epoch, blocking precomputation. An attacker needs one real presence per fake, about $30-$80 a month each, so 100 fakes cost $3,000-$8,000 monthly. Slow links risk false flags, so flagged seats get a bonded appeal with a 500 POA stake.
